headline: A blowout UBL earnings beat gets swamped by an oil-driven risk-off tape — KSE-100 closes down 1,703 points even as Brent eases off its intraday spike.
summary: PSX closed down 0.98% today at 174,429.92 (down 1,703 points) even though Brent eased back to $84.78 after spiking past $92 intraday on a tenth day of US-Iran strikes. The real story: UBL posted a strong H1 profit, up 33% year-on-year, yet its own stock still fell 2% on the day — a clear sign macro fear is beating good company news right now. The regime stays risk-off: high rates, a soft rupee, and oil still up over 8% on the month keep banks and E&P better placed than cement, autos, and fuel retailers, whose costs rise with crude. Banks and E&P remain the desk's preferred ground into the next few sessions.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: High policy rates (11.5%) keep the funding-cost carry trade intact, and UBL's 33% profit jump confirms the sector's earnings engine is healthy even though the stock itself sold off today on macro fear.

sectors.name: E&P (Oil & Gas)
sectors.why: Brent is still up over 8% for the month despite today's pullback to $84.78, and the desk's own risk radar flags E&P (OGDC/PPL/MARI) as a direct beneficiary of the ongoing oil shock.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Demand is domestic and largely insulated from the oil/shipping story — a defensive tilt while the Iran conflict runs into its second week, and FFC has a dated results catalyst on 2026-07-29.

sectors.name: OMCs & Refining
sectors.why: The desk's risk radar names OMCs and cement as the two sectors most exposed to the fuel/energy-cost side of the oil shock — PSO's margins stay thin without E&P's offsetting upside.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Cement is energy-cost sensitive; a firmer oil bill and a soft rupee (277.63, near a one-month high) squeeze input costs just as the sector already sits on the macro desk's avoid list.

sectors.name: Autos & Textiles/Exporters
sectors.why: Imported-input costs rise with the oil bill and a weaker rupee, and the sector is explicitly flagged as unfavoured in the current high-rate, risk-off regime.

watchlist.angle: The desk's OBV-accumulation trigger fired on BML with high confidence — on its own history this setup has won 96.6% of 89 trades (net expectancy +5.11%/trade, still 83% out-of-sample). Fundamentals back it up: cheap at roughly 6.4x earnings with a 32% net margin, and it sits in Commercial Banks, one of the desk's two favoured sectors right now. Live levels: entry 59.25, stop 57.18, target 62.80.
watchlist.risk: A fresh leg down in the oil/Iran story would likely drag banks broadly lower regardless of BML's own setup — the stop is tight relative to entry, so a gap-down open on bad headlines could take it out fast.

watchlist.angle: Today's actual headline story: consolidated H1 profit of Rs85.9bn (EPS Rs34.3), up 33% year-on-year, on record deposits of Rs6.1trn — a genuine earnings beat. The fundamental read is attractive: a fair PE near 8.3x and a dividend yield of 6.75% covered by only about half of profit. That the stock still closed down 2% on the day is itself the day's clearest 'good news, bad tape' example.
watchlist.risk: There's no active technical trigger here — this is a fundamentals-and-news story, not a chart breakout — and Q2 alone showed cost-to-income creeping up (40% vs 33% a year ago) and a heavy 52% effective tax rate, so the quality of the beat isn't spotless. Further oil-driven selling could keep the stock under pressure regardless of the print.

watchlist.angle: Fertilizer is one of the desk's macro-favoured sectors (domestic demand, insulated from the oil-and-shipping story hitting cement and OMCs), FFC sits near the top of the desk's predictability rankings, and it has a real, dated catalyst: results due 2026-07-29.
watchlist.risk: The payout ratio is already high (82%), so a soft results print would test the dividend story the stock is partly priced for.

watchlist.angle: Dolmen City REIT carries a confirmed, dated catalyst: book closure runs 2026-07-25 to 2026-07-27, with today (2026-07-22) the last day to buy and still qualify for the Rs0.66/share dividend (about 1.71% yield). It also tops the desk's predictability screen, and as a rental-income REIT it's less directly exposed to the oil shock than cyclical names.
watchlist.risk: The payout ratio runs over 100% of earnings — a stretched dividend that a soft year could force to be cut — and REIT prices typically adjust down by roughly the dividend amount once the stock goes ex.

watchlist.angle: A Donchian-55 breakout trigger fired on TPLT with the dashboard's high-confidence tag — a strategy that has won 61.5% of past trades on the name (net expectancy +3.62%, 75% hit rate out-of-sample). Live levels: entry 27.91, stop 26.51, target 30.70.
watchlist.risk: The fundamental picture is the opposite of clean: TPLT is currently loss-making with no dividend, small (Rs5.4bn market cap) and higher-beta (1.3x) than the market — this is a pure technical, momentum-driven read, not one backed by the underlying business, and it's the highest-risk name on this list.

catalysts.event: DCR book-closure buy-by (last day to qualify for the Rs0.66/share, ~1.71% yield dividend; book closure runs 2026-07-25 to 2026-07-27)
LOTCHEM ex-dividend/buy-by ahead of its confirmed book closure (2026-07-27 to 2026-07-29, Rs1.5/share, ~5.12% yield)
SBP MPC — first FY27 rate decision; a hold at 11.5% is widely expected (97% of surveyed analysts)
FFC results (also COLG, EFERT, HCAR, JSML — scraped estimates, unconfirmed)

risks: Conflict escalation: a tenth day of US strikes on Iran and Brent's intraday spike past $92 show the oil shock isn't over — a further leg up would deepen import-bill and rupee pressure even after today's pullback to $84.78.
Currency and rates: USD/PKR sits near 277.63 (a one-month high) with CPI still at 11.1% — a weaker rupee keeps the SBP hawkish into the July 27 MPC and is a standing equity headwind.
The UBL pattern — a genuine earnings beat that still closed lower — is a warning that broad macro fear can keep overwhelming individually good company results through the rest of results season.
